facts.title: Starring in "Desperately Seeking Susan" – 1985 Film
facts.body: Madonna starred in the 1985 movie "Desperately Seeking Susan," a film that featured Rockets Redgler, a drug dealer and wannabe actor suspected by some of murdering Nancy Spungen, in a role as a cab driver. "If you ever see the 1985 movie Desperately Seeking Susan starring Madonna, he plays a cab driver."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Sid Vicious
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: The Virgin Tour Ticket Demand & Venue Upgrades (1985)
facts.body: In the two months following her pivotal 1984 MTV Music Awards performance, all tickets for Madonna's upcoming tour, "The Virgin Tour," sold out within days. The demand was so overwhelming that many venues initially planned for her performances proved too small, necessitating changes to larger stadiums to accommodate the massive demand. "Las entradas de su gira se agotaban en días, o sea, en los dos meses posteriores a esa grandísima actuación que hizo los musical awards, se agotaron todas las entradas de todos los conciertos en Madonna."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: Madonna y la provocación
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Top of the Pops Performance & London's Reception (1985)
facts.body: Approximately three months after her controversial MTV Music Awards performance, Madonna was urgently called to the United Kingdom to replicate the exact same performance on "Top of the Pops" in London. Unlike the scandalous reception in the U.S., London audiences and European society, generally more open in the 80s, received her provocation as "fresh air," "new," "provocative," "healthy," and "feminist," fostering a "love story" between Madonna and London. "En el Reino Unido, se recibía como aire fresco, como nuevo, como provocador, como sano, como feminista, la gente se echaba al movimiento."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: Madonna y la provocación
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: The Virgin Tour VHS Success (1985)
facts.body: The concerts during "The Virgin Tour" became so immensely popular and in-demand that pirated recordings circulated rapidly among fans. Recognizing this demand, Madonna and her record label smartly decided to release an official VHS, "Madonna Live: The Virgin Tour," which for a long time became the best-selling music VHS in history. "Así es como acabo saliendo M.V.S.E. en La Icabergi que durante mucho tiempo fue el U.V.S.E. de música más vendido de la historia."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: Madonna y la provocación
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Becoming a Multimillionaire & Icon (1985)
facts.body: By the end of "The Virgin Tour" in 1985, Madonna had achieved two significant milestones: she had become a multimillionaire due to her stadium-filling performances, and she had cemented her status as an absolute symbol of provocation, feminism, freedom, and open expression, firmly establishing herself as the definitive icon of the 1980s. "Madonna ya después en la Icabergi era increíblemente millonaria porque había llegado estadios y la segunda es que Madonna ya era símbolo absoluto de provocación, de feminismo, de libertad, de hablar sin tapujos, Madonna ya era el icono de los 80 que sería para el resto y para siempre."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: Madonna y la provocación
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Record Label Dispute over Singles (1985)
facts.body: Executives at Sire and Geffen Records bickered over which Madonna songs could be released as singles from the "Vision Quest" soundtrack, a situation indicative of her rising "imperiality" due to having "too many hits." This dispute resulted in "Crazy for You" being released by Geffen, while "Gambler" was withheld as a single. "Reportedly, executives at two labels, sire and geffen, bickered with each other over which Madonna songs could be released as singles."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Uninvited to "We Are the World" (1985)
facts.body: Madonna was notably not invited to participate in USA for Africa's "We Are the World" project. The irony was highlighted when her song "Crazy for You" later unseated "We Are the World" from the number one spot, a "giant killing feat" that underscored her ascendant status. "The fact that Madonna was not invited to We Are the World only made the irony more delicious."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: "Into the Groove" Sacrificed for Chart Strategy (1985)
facts.body: Madonna's label chose not to release "Into the Groove" as a single in America, sacrificing what was arguably her "greatest dance floor song" due to label whims and a fear it would divert radio attention from other releases. This act was seen as a "miscarriage of chart justice" but also an "Imperial flex," demonstrating her power within the major label system. "Again, talk about Imperial, Madonna sacrificed a major hit to the whims of the major label system, and not just any hit, arguably her greatest dance floor song."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: The Virgin Tour (1985)
facts.body: This marked Madonna's first headlining tour, during which she filmed the video for her single "Dress You Up." "By then, she was on her first headlining tour, the virgin tour."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Marriage to Sean Penn (August 1985)
facts.body: Madonna married actor Sean Penn in August 1985 in Malibu, an event that became a major tabloid story and a "circus" complete with helicopters flying overhead, significantly contributing to her "center of the culture status." "One other thing that happened to Madonna in her crazy 1985, she married actor Sean Penn."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Material Girl in an Imperial World Edition Part 2
facts.name: Madonna

facts.title: Transition to Drums (1985)
facts.body: Around his 16th birthday in January 1985, as Freak Baby evolved into Mission Impossible, Dave Grohl transitioned from guitar to playing the drums. "By this time, David moved to Drums, and this is where we finally get to Dave's earliest recordings that we can find."

facts.body: The music video for her hit "Freeway of Love" marked Franklin's first appearance on MTV, a significant step in her 1980s comeback and her embrace of the MTV era. "Its video got her on MTV for the first time."

facts.title: Boosting Whitney Houston (1985-1986)
facts.body: Franklin and her "honorary auntie" Whitney Houston, whose mother Cissy sang backup for Franklin for years, mutually boosted each other's chart success. Houston's video for "How Well I Know" even featured a clip of Franklin, providing an implicit seal of approval as Houston brought gospel-trained R&B vocals back to the forefront. "In a way, 22-year-old Whitney and her honorary auntie, Aritha Franklin, boosted each other up the charts that year."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: Say a Little Prayer Edition Part 2

facts.title: Second Wave (Late 1970s-1985)
facts.body: The "second wave" of Ska emerged in the UK in the wake of punk, fueled by Jamaican immigrants who moved to Britain after Jamaica's independence due to a post-war labor shortage. It was initially known as "Bluebeat" and coexisted with R&B, Soul, and Reggae, embraced by British youth subcultures like mods, rockers, teddy boys, and early punks. "The second wave came in the wake of punk. Jamaica became an independent nation in 1962, so no more British colony."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 2:  Ska

facts.title: Michael Stipe's Nervous Breakdown and HIV/AIDS Fears (Leading up to 1985)
facts.body: Michael Stipe experienced a "complete nervous breakdown" leading up to 1985, which went unrecognized by his bandmates, who perceived him as being "impossible." This period was marked by intense fear as a gay man, terrified that his past behaviors would lead to death from AIDS/HIV, a condition not widely discussed at the time. This dread and paranoia, especially during common colds, persisted until he received an anonymous HIV test in 1987. His mental state during this time, coupled with the cold, damp recording conditions in London, notably affected the sound and commercial performance of R.E.M.'s third album, "Fables of the Reconstruction." "Most of the time that I was a pop star, I loved it, but in this period leading up to 1985, I had this complete nervous breakdown and nobody recognized it."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Tales of Weird Rock’n’Roll Sex
facts.name: R.E.M.

facts.title: Acquisition of ATV Music (1985)
facts.body: In 1985, Michael Jackson outbid Paul McCartney to purchase the ATV Music catalog for $47.5 million. This catalog included 4,000 songs, notably 250 by The Beatles (almost their entire output), as well as tracks by The Rolling Stones, Elvis, and Bruce Springsteen. "In 1985, ATV Music, that company with the Beatles publishing, went up for sale. Four thousand songs, including 250 from the Beatles, which is pretty much everything they ever wrote, as well as tracks by the Rolling Stones, Elvis and Bruce Springsteen. Jackson then outbid McCartney, paying $47.5 million for this catalog."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Buying Catalogues - A Primer
facts.name: Michael Jackson

facts.title: Acquisition of Beatles Publishing Catalog (1985)
facts.body: On August 15, 1985, Michael Jackson purchased a substantial portion of The Beatles' publishing catalog, granting him significant control over their music. This ownership allowed him to authorize the licensing of "Revolution" for the controversial 1987 Nike commercial, despite the objections of the surviving Beatles. "Because on August 15, 1985, he'd bought a huge chunk of the Beatles publishing catalog right out from underneath Paul McCartney's nose."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Concept of Selling Out: Part 1
facts.name: Michael Jackson

facts.title: "Computer Reggae" Shift (1985)
facts.body: The landscape of reggae on black radio began to transform around 1985 with the advent of "computer reggae," a subgenre that incorporated sounds more akin to hip hop, thereby making it more accessible and appealing to a broader black audience. "That began to change in 1985 with what he called computer reggae, which sounded more like hip hop."

facts.title: Deep Six Compilation (1985) – First Soundgarden Recordings
facts.body: The original 1984 lineup of Soundgarden (Cornell, Yamamoto, Sundquist on drums, and Kim Thayil on guitar) recorded their first material in 1985. Three tracks appeared on a compilation called *Deep Six* issued by Seattle's CZ Records, including a track called "Here We Tick." "That would be the original lineup of Soundgarden from 1984."

facts.title: Management by Susan Silver (1985-1998)
facts.body: Susan Silver started managing Soundgarden in 1985, formalizing the arrangement by 1986. Her initial motivation was a "starry-eyed idea of helping bands reach their dreams." Silver continued to manage the band until 1998, a year after their 1997 breakup, at which point she shut down her company, Silver Management.
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Mighty Managers of Rock

facts.title: Initiating "A View to a Kill" Theme (1985)
facts.body: The idea for Duran Duran to create the "A View to a Kill" theme originated with their bass player, Roger Taylor. While reportedly drunk at a party, Taylor approached producer Cubby Broccoli and challenged him about getting "someone decent to do one of your theme songs," an unexpected approach that surprisingly led to the band getting the commission. "Actually it was bass player Roger Taylor who had the idea. He was drunk at a party and he wandered up to producer Cubby Broccoli and said something very close to this. When are you going to get someone decent to do one of your theme songs?"
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Bond...James Bond...Music

facts.title: Controversial Senate Testimony (1985)
facts.body: During his 1985 Senate testimony, Frank Zappa became very angry, yelling and making macabre comparisons between censorship and Hitler's anti-Jewish murders, which ultimately did not greatly aid the cause against censorship. facts.title: Grandstanding at Live Aid (July 13, 1985)
facts.body: During U2's performance of "Bad" at Live Aid, Bono engaged in an extended moment trying to pull a dance partner from the audience, consuming many minutes of their allotted time. This "grandstanding" caused the band to miss playing their biggest hit, "Pride (In the Name of Love)," and led to a major backstage confrontation. "Donald decided he needed a dance partner and spent many long minutes trying to pull somebody out of the audience."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1
facts.name: Bono

facts.title: Alleged Quit Threat Post-Live Aid (July 13, 1985)
facts.body: Following a heated argument backstage after U2's Live Aid set, Bono allegedly told the band, "fine, I quit," expressing his frustration with the situation. "Emotions got out of control, and Bono allegedly said, fine, I quit."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1
facts.name: Bono

facts.title: Reconsideration and Apology After Live Aid (July 13, 1985)
facts.body: After allegedly quitting U2 following Live Aid, Bono flew back to Dublin alone and took a long drive to calm down. During this drive, he reportedly picked up a female hitchhiker who recognized him and praised U2's performance. This conversation prompted Bono to reconsider his decision, leading him to apologize to the other band members in Dublin and ask to be allowed back into the group. "This conversation made Bono think that maybe he had been a little hasty in quitting."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1

"Donald decided he needed a dance partner and spent many long minutes trying to pull somebody out of the audience."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1
facts.name: Bono

facts.title: Reconsideration and Apology After Live Aid (July 13, 1985)
facts.body: After allegedly quitting U2 following Live Aid, Bono flew back to Dublin alone and took a long drive to calm down. During this drive, he reportedly picked up a female hitchhiker who recognized him and praised U2's performance. This conversation prompted Bono to reconsider his decision, leading him to apologize to the other band members in Dublin and ask to be allowed back into the group. "This conversation made Bono think that maybe he had been a little hasty in quitting."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 1
facts.name: Bono

facts.title: North London Polytechnic Riot (March 15, 1985)
facts.body: This infamous gig became known as "the great Jesus and Marychain riot." The band, having recently moved from Scotland to London, had a hit single "Never Understand." Promoters oversold tickets, leading to an impatient, cramped, and surly crowd. After an opening band member threw a bottle at the audience, the crowd erupted. The Jesus and Mary Chain then kept the audience waiting an hour before playing a 20-minute, feedback-laden set and leaving, prompting the crowd to throw beer cans, invade the stage, and smash all the band's gear. The event received significant media attention due to the presence of the British music press. "The Jesus and Marychain provocateurs of the Great Riots at North London Polytechnic on March 15th, 1985."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Legendary Gigs
facts.name: The Jesus and Mary Chain

facts.title: Ricky Wilson's AIDS-Related Illness and Death (October 12, 1985)
facts.body: Ricky Wilson, the guitarist for The B-52s, became the first notable musician to die from AIDS on October 12, 1985, just nine days after actor Rock Hudson's passing. He had been ill since 1983 and experienced severe health issues throughout most of 1985, including Kaposi's sarcoma, infections, and pneumonia. Due to the pervasive stigma associated with AIDS and gay men at the time, Wilson kept his condition private, with his sister and bandmate, Cindy Wilson, only learning of his diagnosis three days before his death. He passed away at Sloan Kettering Hospital in New York at the age of 32. "Ricky Wilson became the first notable musician to die of AIDS."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: From the Archives: The Top 100 Moments in New Rock - Part 3
facts.name: The B‐52s

facts.title: Financial Turnaround and Death (1985-1997)
facts.body: Richard Berry experienced a dramatic financial turnaround, going from $240 a month on welfare in 1985 to earning $160,000 from "Louie Louie" in 1989. He died in 1997, "happy, respected and wealthy," having finally received deserved credit and recognition for his musical contributions. "He didn't get any back payment from what the song had already earned, but he went from getting $240 a month on welfare in 1985, to making $160,000 from Louis Louis in 1989 which had Berry died in 1997, happy, respected and wealthy."
facts.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
facts.episode: Episode 106:"Louie Louie" by the Kingsmen

facts.title: 39th Birthday Party in Munich (1985)
facts.body: Freddie Mercury's 39th birthday celebration in Munich in 1985 is considered one of the two greatest parties in rock history. He invited all his friends to a costume party, and the images from this event, including guests arriving in horse-drawn carriages and the extravagant costumes, are iconic. It is often compared to Grace Jones's party at Studio 54 where Mick Jagger ended up hospitalized. "La grandísima fiesta de cumpleaños quiso Freddy Mercury en 1985. Son las dos mayores fiestas de la historia de Rock."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: QUEEN como iconografía estética y gráfica
facts.name: Freddie Mercury

facts.title: Live Aid (1985) Iconic Outfit
facts.body: Freddie Mercury's outfit at the Live Aid concert in 1985, consisting of white trousers with a red stripe and a yellow military-style jacket, has become an iconic piece of rock fashion. This look has been reinterpreted and referenced by various designers, such as Yves Saint Laurent and Martin Margiela, over the past 30 years. "El propio Freddy Mercury en el concierto de Life Aid, desde el pantalón Blanco con una banda roja hasta la cazadora Casa Cada Marilla que han sido versionados por distintos diseñadores como Isalora Go Martin Margel en los últimos 30 años."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: QUEEN como iconografía estética y gráfica
facts.name: Freddie Mercury

facts.title: Nervous Breakdown and HIV/AIDS Anxiety (Leading up to 1985-1987)
facts.body: Michael Stipe suffered a "complete nervous breakdown" leading up to 1985, which his bandmates misconstrued as him being "impossible." During this period, he was consumed by terror, believing his past behaviors as a gay man would lead to his death from AIDS/HIV. This paranoia manifested as dread with every cold until he underwent an anonymous HIV test in 1987. This emotional turmoil significantly impacted the recording of R.E.M.'s third album, "Fables of the Reconstruction," contributing to it being the band's least favorite and a commercial disappointment. "Until it was finally able to get an anonymous HIV test in 1987, there was a sense of dread and paranoia every time I got a cold."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Tales of Weird Rock’n’Roll Sex
facts.name: Michael Stipe

facts.body: Released in 1985, *Brothers in Arms* is widely recognized as the first AAD album. The recording process was analog, but the mastering and mixing were done digitally, and the physical format was digital. Its status as the "first" is controversial due to the progressive integration of digital effects into many analog recordings, blurring the exact line of transition. "Llegamos a 1985 cuando sale Brothers In Hals de Dades Trades, que se considera el primer disco a de... se grabó en analógico, pero el proceso de masterización y mezclado ya era digital y se hacían formatos digitales el formato físico."
facts.source: Music Radar Clan
facts.episode: El cambio de Musica analogica a musica digital.
facts.name: Brothers in Arms

facts.body: This album, Dire Straits' fifth studio effort, was recorded at Air Studios on the island of Montserrat. It became a global number one smash, topping charts around the world, including in America, and sold more than 30 million copies. It featured guest harmony vocals from Sting on the track "Money for Nothing." "Money for Nothing and the Brothers in Arms LP wound up topping charts around the world, including in America, and sold more than 30 million copies."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.title: Most Albums in Shortest Period (1985-1987)
facts.body: The British industrial outfit Psychic TV holds the official Guinness Book of World Records record for releasing the greatest number of albums over the shortest period of time. Between 1985 and early 1987, an eighteen-month span, the band released an astonishing 14 albums. While most of these were live recordings of varying quality, the achievement stands as a world record. "During one eighteen-month spurt that stretched from 1985 to early 1987, they released 14 albums. It's true that most of these releases were live recordings of sketchy quality, but that's the official world record in the Guinness Book."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The Book of World Records Version 1.0 - Part 1
facts.name: Psychic TV

facts.title: Sale of Catalog to Michael Jackson (1985)
facts.body: In 1985, ATV Music, holding 4,000 songs including 250 by The Beatles and tracks by The Rolling Stones, Elvis, and Bruce Springsteen, was sold to Michael Jackson for $47.5 million. "In 1985, ATV Music, that company with the Beatles publishing, went up for sale. Four thousand songs, including 250 from the Beatles, which is pretty much everything they ever wrote, as well as tracks by the Rolling Stones, Elvis and Bruce Springsteen. Jackson then outbid McCartney, paying $47.5 million for this catalog."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Buying Catalogues - A Primer
facts.name: ATV Music

facts.body: This "blockbuster hit" had just dropped from the number one spot when it featured Sting on harmony vocals. Sting also incorporated a counter melody later in the song, which he borrowed from a previous hit by The Police. "Just a few spots higher, a blockbuster hit by the British band, Dyer Straits, that had just fallen out of the number one spot, included harmony vocals from none other than Sting. On Money for Nothing, not only did Sting pitch in on the song's chorus, later in the song, he also sneaked in this counter melody."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

facts.body: This song was famously written by Mark Knopfler after he observed workmen at a New York appliance store watching MTV and making snide remarks about musicians. While Dire Straits were recording it at Air Studios in Montserrat, Sting, who was vacationing on the island, was invited to add harmony vocals. His contribution, particularly a riff on the "I want my MTV" slogan (sung to the tune of The Police's "Don't Stand So Close To Me"), earned him a co-songwriting and publishing credit, generating significant income. The song, along with the "Brothers in Arms" album, became a global number one hit. "Famously, Knopfler wrote money for nothing. After observing some workmen at a New York appliance store watching MTV and making snide remarks about how easy it must be to be a musician."
facts.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
facts.episode: If You Love Sting, Set Him Free Edition Part 2
facts.name: Money for Nothing

facts.body: This song was rated very low by students who scored high on the psychopathy scale in a New York University study. The research explored musical preferences among individuals with psychopathic tendencies, finding this track unpopular with that group. "These same people rated songs like Money for Nothing by Dire Straits, and the next My Shirona really low, same thing with classical music they didn't like it."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition
